purpose: How quickly can this voice produce its first usable audio buffer? This isolates generation from the separate wait for playback and sound.
method: Known English text is sent through the actual native voice adapter after preparation. Five back-to-back warm same-text requests are summarized separately from the first synthesis after preparation.
The clock stops at the first nonempty generated PCM buffer. It does not stop at a speaker, a microphone, or the end of a conversational turn.
findings: All five generation results are saved individually. Speaker output and ASR-plus-voice qualification remain pending; no fastest-audible default has been selected.
Generated audio can be ready before playback starts. Use the separate physical speaker reports before drawing a conclusion about how quickly someone hears this voice.
